facts.value: This is the Lothian Valuation Joint Board's own Unaudited Annual Accounts 2025/26, Treasury Management report 2025/26 and Revenue Budget 2026/27 Update — presented to the Board on 8 June 2026. It is served from City of Edinburgh Council's ModernGov site because the Council provides the Treasurer function to the LVJB (Treasurer: Richard Lloyd-Bithell, p.1). The paper's GSS in the queue is S12000036 (City of Edinburgh) but the paper is NOT the City of Edinburgh Council's own treasury report — it is the annual return of the LVJB, a separately constituted joint valuation board serving Edinburgh, East Lothian, Midlothian and West Lothian. Same shape as the Buckinghamshire Fire Authority for BUC and the Bedford PCC for BED (EMAIL_TEMPLATE.md §8 near-identical-names trap). 4-page covering report; the Appendix 1 (Unaudited Annual Accounts) is NOT bundled.

source.title: Unaudited Annual Accounts 2025/26, Treasury Management report 2025/26 and Revenue Budget 2026/27 Update — Lothian Valuation Joint Board, 8 June 2026

facts.note: Read as if it were an Edinburgh Council paper it would put another body's numbers in front of Edinburgh's S151. No word of 'PWLB', 'loan', 'borrowing', 'CFR', 'MRP', 'maturity', 'HRA', 'liability benchmark' or 'prudential' appears anywhere.

facts.value: LVJB reported expenditure of £7.200m for 2025/26. Net contribution of £0.254m from usable reserves. Closing usable reserve £0.665m. Accounts authorised for issue 2 June 2026; Audit Scotland to present the ISA 260 to Governance on 16 November 2026. Treasurer's opinion: reasonable assurance on internal control system.
facts.note: Joint valuation board figures, not the City of Edinburgh Council's.

facts.value: General reserve £0.665m at 31 March 2026: £0.201m minimum-reserve commitment (3% of core budget requisitions); £0.162m earmarked for future NDR Reform costs; £0.130m earmarked for South Gyle lease property costs. Approved 2026/27 revenue budget requires net drawdown of £0.172m from the General reserve.

LVJB does not borrow in its own right. It maintains cash management as part of the City of Edinburgh Council's group of bank accounts. Any cash balance is effectively lent to the Council and offset by Council expenditure incurred on the Board's behalf. Interest is given on month-end net indebtedness. For 2025/26 interest was calculated per the (withdrawn) LASAAC Guidance Note 2 on Interest on Revenue Balances.
facts.note: This is the entire treasury content of the paper. No external debt, no counterparty list beyond the host Council, no maturity profile, no investment mandate.

facts.value: Net end-of-month balances due to LVJB for 2025/26 (§4.11 page 3, £): Opening 1,029,263; 30 Apr 1,092,151; 31 May 955,603; 30 Jun 1,220,639; 31 Jul 1,292,746; 31 Aug 949,497; 30 Sep 1,108,107; 31 Oct 1,054,833; 30 Nov 945,367; 31 Dec 507,741; 31 Jan 2026 736,311; 28 Feb 2026 707,631; 31 Mar 2026 693,336. Range £0.508m – £1.293m across the year; balance runs down through the second half.
facts.note: The £0.786m fall from November to December is not explained in the paper.

facts.value: Interest calculated on the average monthly balance. Interest rate applied: 3.663%. Interest payment: £35,407 (§4.12 page 3).

2026/27 revenue budget approved 2 February 2026. Scottish Government budget included £5m of additional 2026/27 revenue funding for a targeted Council Tax revaluation of dwellings valued above £1m, to support two new high-value Council Tax bands from 1 April 2028. LVJB's share now confirmed at £1,645,806, paid to City of Edinburgh Council and passed through in full. Assessor awaits final Terms of Reference from the Scottish Government; recommendation 1.4 grants delegated authority to incur essential project expenditure pending detailed budget plan.
facts.note: Interesting Scottish policy context (two new high-value CT bands from April 2028) but no bearing on any council's treasury position and outside the platform's scope.

facts.value: CANNOT be checked. The paper prints no CFR, no external borrowing figure, no OLTL and no internal-borrowing figure. LVJB carries none of these because it does not borrow. Edinburgh's own balance sheet is not in this paper.

summary.text:
Wrong body, thin paper. This document is served from the City of Edinburgh Council's ModernGov site because the Council provides the Treasurer function to the Lothian Valuation Joint Board, but the paper is the LVJB's own Unaudited Annual Accounts, Treasury Management report and Revenue Budget update — not the City of Edinburgh Council's. Same shape as the Buckinghamshire Fire Authority sitting under BUC or the Bedford PCC sitting under BED, and the same trap. Read as an Edinburgh paper it would put another body's numbers in front of Edinburgh's S151.

The LVJB does not borrow in its own right. Its treasury activity is confined to a running cash balance held with the host Council under intra-group arrangements: any cash is effectively lent to the Council, offset by expenditure the Council undertakes on the Board's behalf, and interest is paid on the month-end net indebtedness. For 2025/26 the balance ran between £0.508m and £1.293m and interest of £35,407 was paid at 3.663% on the average monthly balance. The Board reported expenditure of £7.200m, drew £0.254m from usable reserves and closed with a £0.665m general reserve, of which all but about £0.172m is already earmarked (3% minimum + NDR Reform + South Gyle). The 2026/27 budget draws a further £0.172m — leaving essentially no unearmarked reserve at year-end 2026/27 on paper, but at this scale of accounting (£0.5–0.9m against £7.2m of expenditure) it is an LVJB governance point, not a treasury one, and not a City of Edinburgh matter.

The words PWLB, loan, borrowing, CFR, MRP, maturity, HRA, liability benchmark and prudential do not appear anywhere in the four pages. There is no external debt figure, no CFR, no MRP policy, no maturity profile, no counterparty list beyond the host Council, no borrowing plan and no rate assumptions. The balance-sheet identity cannot be checked because none of its inputs is printed.

Our PWLB file for the City of Edinburgh Council is recorded here for completeness only: 104 loans totalling £1,729,433,511 at a weighted 3.9488% at 31 March 2026, sitting on an indicative £226m discount against the DMO's 14 August 2026 curve. Reconciliation against this paper is not possible because the paper prints no Edinburgh Council loan-book figure to reconcile against. Quoting these numbers back from this paper would misrepresent an LVJB return as an Edinburgh treasury report, which it is not.

No email drafted. This paper gives no basis for first-contact with the Edinburgh S151 about the Council's treasury. The right next step, if Edinburgh coverage is a priority, is the City of Edinburgh Council's own Treasury Management Annual Report 2025/26 or Treasury Management Strategy 2026/27 to the Finance and Resources Committee or Full Council. Neither is on disk.
